page: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.4xlarge is an instance within the High Performance Computing family engineered for compute- and memory-intensive distributed workloads. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, the instance supplies 16 dedicated physical cores on 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-V1 processors running at 2.6 GHz. Simultaneous multithreading is disabled, allowing each of the 16 vCPUs direct execution access to individual cores backed by 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core alongside 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 128.0 GB, providing an allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The instance provides 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage volumes, and includes no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable memory subsystem throughput alongside steady compute capabilities. In testing, hpc7g.4xlarge achieved a PassMark memory score of 3147.16 and recorded 97.55 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory write bandwidth. General multi-core processing tests, such as Geekbench multi-core at 13150.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 24504.24, demonstrate consistent execution across dedicated ARM cores. Specialized cryptographic performance and large language model inference place lower, with PassMark CPU encryption reaching 2231.53 and large-model generation measuring 2.3 tokens per second.

The absence of integrated local storage necessitates network storage solutions for persistent data, while the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio and 200 Gbps interconnect optimize multi-node scale-out configurations. These architectural parameters position the hpc7g.4xlarge for tightly coupled scientific modeling, computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, and parallelized engineering simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.4xlarge is an ARM-based compute instance built for high-performance computing workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro system, the server features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by AWS Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz, completely avoiding simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and connects to a 200 Gbps baseline network fabric. There are no attached local storage disks and no hardware accelerators. Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory performance, achieving 97.55 GB/sec in large-block write bandwidth and a PassMark memory score of 3147.16, alongside average general multi-core compute capability. Conversely, encryption and large-model inference tests rank in lower percentiles. The hpc7g.4xlarge is well aligned for coupled scientific simulations, computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, and parallel batch workloads requiring high-bandwidth memory and node-to-node network communications.
